paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens for the baseline Mistral-v0.2-Base model (light blue bars) and the same model fine-tuned on data from six different clinical specialties: Cardio (light peach), Gastro (peach), Infect (orange), Neuro (dark orange), Obstetrics (brown), and Pediatrics (dark brown). The horizontal axis, labeled "Per-specialty terms," displays six groups of bars, each corresponding to one of the specialties (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), arranged in that order. The vertical axis, labeled "Negative log probability," is scaled linearly from -22 to -27, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Within each group, the baseline model’s bar (light blue) is consistently the shortest, indicating the highest negative log-probability (i.e., lowest probability of generating relevant tokens) across all specialties. The fine-tuned models show progressively taller bars (lower negative log-probabilities, meaning higher token probabilities) within their respective specialty groups; for example, the Pediatrics fine-tuned model (dark brown) shows the tallest bar in the Pediatrics group, while the Neuro fine-tuned model (dark orange) shows the tallest bar in the Neuro group. In general, the fine-tuned models exhibit improved performance (lower negative log-probabilities) in their corresponding specialty, with the most significant improvements observed when the model is fine-tuned on the same specialty as the test tokens. The bars are grouped by specialty and sorted in the same order as the x-axis labels, with no visual emphasis or annotations applied to specific bars.
